position_in_era.primary_genre_lineage: flamenco × trap / pop / R&B / reggaeton (Gen Z translation)
position_in_era.historical_role: The canonical Gen Z flamenco re-frame. *El Mal Querer* was Rosalía's flamenco-studies thesis at ESMUC under Chiqui de la Línea, released as a major-label album. 'Malamente' opens with a clear bulería compás laid as the foundation of trap palmas — the single most-cited example in the 2010s of flamenco vocabulary translated into pop electronics with both languages still audibly separable.

narrative_slots.production_facts: Released 2 November 2018 on Sony / Columbia. Co-produced by Rosalía and El Guincho. Conceived as her ESMUC final-degree project on Catalan / Andalusian flamenco modernity.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Rosalía Vila Tobella studied under flamenco master José Miguel Vizcaya 'Chiqui de la Línea' at ESMUC; producer El Guincho (Pablo Díaz-Reixa) as principal collaborator.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: Catalonia (Rosalía's home) — significant because Rosalía came to flamenco from outside the Andalusian-Romani inherited line, parallel to Dorantes' move to bring piano (a non-flamenco instrument) into the centre of flamenco.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Bulería palmas as base for trap kicks; 12/8 bulería compás; tangos, fandangos, pregones across the album. Modified samples of Justin Timberlake's 'Cry Me a River' on 'Bagdad'.
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: Multiple Latin Grammys, including Album of the Year (the first flamenco-rooted album to win in that category).
